items.summary: Risk disposition: blocked for public launch, monetization expansion, notification expansion, and rights outreach; conditional only for ordinary reversible work that preserves existing consent, disclosures, provenance, claims, copyright/trademark, platform-policy, and age-sensitive boundaries. Keep searchwoot.com private and preview-only. Evidence: Woot documentation confirms API access but not redistribution, storage, derivatives, public display, alerts, affiliate, or advertising rights; current public terms restrict commercial/public product-data use. Fleet compliance is 35 pass, 20 fail, and 6 unknown of 61; security and operations sweeps are unavailable; accuracy, measurement, and owner gates remain incomplete. Exact decision: no public launch or monetization change. Next evidence action: create one dated read-only bundle covering source rights, data flow/retention, GA4 consent/configuration, and logs/vendors/incident handling, then route rights and jurisdictional issues to human counsel.

Launch-readiness tracking remains active. Progress: repository artifacts partially support the data-flow and consent reviews, and public privacy, cookie, and terms pages are identified. No task is closed because required evidence is incomplete. Next action: attach a dated consolidated evidence bundle and preserve all open task statuses.

Revenue disposition: Amazon evidence is limited to 2026-09-21: 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 commission. The $4.92 is entirely in the aggregate other row and cannot be assigned to a site. Do not claim site revenue, ROI, contribution margin, or causal lift. Preserve registered tracking IDs for future links.

For complicated.work, deadlymaracas.com, and driveford.net, retain the concrete decision: parked, private, preview-only, and unlaunched. No publish, deployment, DNS change, analytics configuration, monetization, spending, dependency addition, or queue admission is cleared. Next evidence action: attach dated ownership, preview/build, compliance, security, measurement-boundary, rollback, and explicit-blocker evidence.
